tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the higher Mythos 5 tier in mid-June, billing the Mythos-class model as made safe for general use, though launch coverage immediately flagged controversial usage terms; an early hands-on found Fable 5 "relentlessly proactive." Then on Jun 13 the story turned: a US government export-control directive, citing national security, suspended access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and industry coverage reframed the launch as models deemed too dangerous to release. A later recap framed the takedown as a temporary suspension.
whats_new: An outside recap from InfoQ is the first to characterize the takedown as a temporary suspension — tying it to a US export-control directive — rather than a permanent pull.
why_it_matters: A top-tier model can go from general-availability launch to government-ordered suspension within days, and even a 'temporary' status leaves re-enablement uncertain.

status.detail: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launched "made safe for general use," then a US export-control directive pulled access on national-security grounds. Latest framing: the takedown is a temporary suspension, not a permanent pull.

beats.summary: National-security grounds; reframed industry-wide as "too dangerous to release."

beats.headline: Reframed as a temporary suspension — re-enable date unknown
beats.summary: First source to tie the suspension to the export-control directive and frame it as temporary rather than permanent.

open_questions: Is "temporary" confirmed — does any re-enable date appear?
Does the export-control directive extend to other frontier labs?
How are downstream products handling the sudden loss of access?
take_for_builders: A flagship can go GA → government-suspended in days. Keep a fallback model wired in rather than hard-coding a single flagship tier into production.
